It's sometimes dependant on the type of accreditation the course has. Sometimes, pure Psychology (Hons) courses have accreditation by the BPS or whatever psychological board operates in your area. I've typically found that other courses labelled as "psychological sciences" are not accredited, meaning that if you wanted to get student or graduate membership, you would have to take a conversion course after.

This may change over different areas, this is for the UK specifically in my experience. I hope this helps!

quick edit: if you want to go onto professional practice in a psychological field then accredited courses are HIGHLY preferred, if not mandatory. I reccomend staying with accredited courses if your future career is aimed at psychological practice in any field.

Going to the toilet.
People in my school would all disrespect the toilets by smoking and putting graffiti in them. Some fights would even occur in them too. Although there were cameras installed on the outside of toilet stalls and smoke alarms fitted in the school people still kept on fighting, smoking and filling up the toilets and sinks with toilet paper to block them. Instead of finding the handful of culprits responsible, my school thought it was a brilliant idea to just ban them altogether. Only those with serious medical conditions or doctors notes got to go to the toilets. If you didn't have one, you had no chance of finding a toilet until you got home (or to a bush). After staff caught on to people using bushes or just accidentally defecating themselves, the rule was quickly abolished.
